storiesSection.title: Stories of Resilience from Inside the Hub
storiesSection.subtitle: Behind every workstation is a student or creator refusing to surrender their future.

items.name: Amal Shawa
items.highlight: After losing my home and living in a tent, I didn't know how I would continue my education. Gaza Educational Center provided me with a place where I can study, attend my classes, and complete my university degree.
items.story: After our displacement, I lost my home and began living in a tent with my family. Our access to basic necessities like electricity and clean water was extremely limited, making continuing my university studies very difficult. I registered at Gaza Educational Center and was accepted. Thanks to a space equipped with reliable power, internet, and a peaceful study environment, I was able to continue my university education, submit assignments, and attend online lectures.
items.quote: After losing my home and living in a tent, I didn't know how I would continue my education. Gaza Educational Center provided me with a place where I can study, attend my classes, and complete my university degree.

items.name: Ahmed Al-Najjar
items.highlight: With continuous blackouts, I was at risk of losing my senior university year. The stable high-speed link allowed me to submit my capstone project and pass finals.
items.story: Amidst the complete blackout, the center provided me with reliable solar power and satellite connectivity daily, enabling me to attend classes and complete my graduation requirements.
items.quote: Due to relentless power outages in our neighborhood, I was about to lose my final academic year. The reliable high-speed connection allowed me to submit my graduation capstone and attend exams.

items.name: Maryam Khalil
items.highlight: The hub was my only sanctuary to fulfill design contracts with overseas clients and upload large files. The income enabled me to support my family.
items.story: Remote freelancing is our primary lifeline. Thanks to the uninterrupted Starlink connection, I maintained international client work and secured our family's daily necessities.
items.quote: EduHub was my only sanctuary to deliver design deliverables to international clients and upload massive project files. The remote income I earned here allowed me to sustain my entire family.

faqSection.title: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Is reserving desks and internet truly free for students?
items.answer: Yes, workstations, stable electricity, and satellite internet are 100% free for university students, recent graduates, and freelancers.

items.question: How do I reach the center and what are the booking conditions?
items.answer: The center is located on Al-Wehda Street, Sondos Building (1st Floor). Booking requires prior reservation via the website to receive an entry code and adhere to reserved time slots.

items.question: How can I donate and verify my support reaches the hub?
items.answer: You can donate directly through the official 100% fee-free Zeffy platform. All contributions go directly to maintain Starlink satellite subscriptions, backup fuel, and solar panels.

items.question: What happens during unexpected power or telecom emergencies?
items.answer: The hub operates a dedicated power system with generators to assure continuous 100% uptime for electricity and internet without any interruptions.
